Interactive drift report as one HTML file

Source: R/drift_viz.R
drfthtml.Rd

Writes a cpsdrft() result to a single web page for a reader who will not run R. Everything is inside the file: the stylesheet, a short script, and the binned summaries of each column as JSON. Nothing is fetched, so the page opens from disk (file://) and looks the same later.

Usage

drfthtml(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Drift report",
  warn = NULL,
  fail = NULL,
  open = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A cpsdrft() result. Attach a provenance record as x$provenance (for example from loadprov()) and an mnfdiff() as x$manifest to show them; rmbl drift --html does both.

file

The path to write.

title

The page title, a string.

warn, fail

The PSI bands the page opens with; NULL (the default) takes the object's bands.

open

Logical: open the page in the browser when written (default FALSE).

Value

The path file, invisibly.

Details

The page shows:

  • a header with the overall verdict, the count of columns per verdict, the row counts, when the page was written, the package version, and the capsule's provenance (name, source, pinned SHA-256, data date) when x$provenance holds one;

  • the column table: verdict, column, type, test (KS for numbers and dates, chi-square homogeneity for categories), statistic, p-value, PSI, the change in the missing share and both sample sizes. It has a search box, filters by verdict and type, and sorts on any header;

  • for the column chosen (click a row, or the up and down keys; / goes to the search box): both samples' summary statistics, or the ten largest categories; their distributions overlaid; each bin's term of the PSI, drawn up where the current sample has more mass and down where it has less; for a numeric column the first digits against Benford's law; and a sentence on what the verdict means;

  • sliders for the warn and fail PSI bands and for alpha, which score the verdicts again as they move, and a button back to the object's bands;

  • a manifest tab with the resources added, removed or changed, their digests and sizes, when x$manifest holds an mnfdiff();

  • a history tab: pick earlier rmbl drift --json outputs or this page's JSON exports, and the PSI of each column is drawn over the runs, points above the fail band marked;

  • exports: Markdown, JSON, each chart as SVG, and the column table copied as a GitHub comment.

The verdicts: fail when the test rejects at alpha, or the PSI is above the fail band with both samples at least psiminn; warn when the PSI is above the warn band; untested when no test applies; ok otherwise. At the object's bands fail is cpsdrft()'s drifted. Each verdict is written in words beside its symbol, the tables have header cells, and each chart has a text label. A light or dark theme follows the system and a button switches it. Every value is escaped. The page holds no rows of the data, only the summaries in x$summ, so its size grows with the number of columns and categories, not of rows.

Errors: x not from cpsdrft(); file not one path; title not one string; warn above fail.

See also

drftapp() for the same report as a Shiny app, plot() for the same charts in base graphics.

Examples

set.seed(5)
ref <- data.frame(value = stats::rnorm(400),
                  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 400, TRUE))
cur <- data.frame(value = stats::rnorm(400, 0.4),
                  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 400, TRUE))
d <- cpsdrft(ref, cur)
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "drift.html")
drfthtml(d, f, title = "Pinned against fetched")
file.exists(f)
#> [1] TRUE

# narrower bands open the page with more columns to look at
drfthtml(d, f, warn = 0.02, fail = 0.05)
unlink(f)
try(drfthtml(list(), f))
#> Error : drfthtml: `x` must be a bricklayer_drift object from cpsdrft()
